Portfolio Analysis

Running a portfolio well comes down to a balance between leverage (LTV) and liquidity (cashflow). Here's how to read your dashboard metrics against the current UK market.

Aggregate LTV Strategy

Lenders look at your whole portfolio as one entity, not property by property.

  • Below 60%: You're in the "Growth Zone." You likely have real equity available to release for further deposits, and you'll usually see the most competitive rates here.
  • 60% - 75%: The "Standard Zone," where most lenders are comfortable. It balances risk and return reasonably well.
  • Above 75%: The "Risk Zone." Refinancing can get harder if property values move against you, so paying down capital here helps keep the portfolio stable.

True Net Cashflow

The Net Cashflow figure on your dashboard is your operational baseline (Rent minus Mortgage). To get to what you'd actually take home, it's worth factoring in a few more costs:

  • Void Provision: Typically 5-10% of gross rent.
  • Maintenance: Setting aside 10% for repairs is the industry standard.
  • Management: Letting agent fees, usually 10-15% + VAT.

A Note on Section 24 (Tax)

If you own personally, mortgage interest relief is capped at the basic rate (20%). If you're a higher-rate taxpayer, that can compress your real yield significantly, so it's worth keeping an eye on your Gross Yield. In today's higher interest rate environment, many investors now need yields of 6%+ to keep the numbers working after tax.

Security Note: Your portfolio data stays in your browser, kept there for privacy. It's never sent to our servers.
